title: FastAPI: typed boundaries, dependencies and service tests
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects fastapi: typed boundaries, dependencies and service tests with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Run integration cases against all domain endpoints using synthetic data.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An AI service should expose typed domain contracts rather than raw provider messages. FastAPI routes accept request models, call application services and return response models. Dependency injection supplies authenticated principals and adapters. Health reports process liveness; readiness reports whether required dependencies can serve requests.

Asynchronous routes help with I/O, but blocking CPU work still occupies execution resources. Offload training and long evaluations to bounded workers or jobs rather than running them on the request event loop.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: The shared service exposes /health, /chat, /classify-failure, /search-failures, /generate-tests and /evaluate. Requests forbid unexpected fields, cap input sizes and carry request IDs. Responses include mode, evidence, status and trace references.

Use dependency overrides for fixture adapters in tests, and exercise real HTTP serialization through TestClient or ASGI transport. Map invalid input to 422, denied access to 403 and unavailable dependencies to a controlled 503. Never return raw exception strings containing secrets.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A route returns any dict and accidentally includes provider credentials in an error response. Another declares async while calling a blocking network client. A health check makes a paid model request and becomes both slow and unreliable.
Test response schemas, extra fields, auth, dependency failure, timeout and cancellation. Verify OpenAPI matches actual responses and that a readiness failure does not imply process death.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Run integration cases against all domain endpoints using synthetic data. Measure contract behavior separately from model accuracy and record adapter mode. Deployment evidence includes typed OpenAPI, bounded work, redacted errors and startup checks.
For SDETs, the AI boundary is familiar API testing with additional uncertainty inside the adapter. Stable service contracts should remain deterministic even when model wording varies.

mistake: A route returns any dict and accidentally includes provider credentials in an error response. Another declares async while calling a blocking network client. A health check makes a paid model request and becomes both slow and unreliable.
takeaway: Run integration cases against all domain endpoints using synthetic data.

title: Request and response models: strict types at the boundary
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects request and response models: strict types at the boundary with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance includes request rejection, response schema conformance and domain evidence checks.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A request model defines which fields a client may supply, their types and bounds. A response model defines which domain fields may leave the service. Forbid extras when unknown fields could smuggle credentials, tenant identity or operational controls. Type validation and business invariants remain separate layers.
Strictness must be deliberate. Coercing a numeric string for ingestion can be useful, but coercing an approval flag from a nonempty string can authorize the wrong action.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use Pydantic ConfigDict(extra='forbid'), bounded strings and closed mode/category enums. Validate live provider outputs again at the domain boundary, resolve evidence IDs and apply UNKNOWN/review rules. Response filtering prevents accidental internal fields from leaking.

The fixture API rejects an api_key field in classification requests and derives tenant identity through a dependency. Source IDs select the immutable authorized log rather than trusting a caller's unrelated text.
sections.code:
from pydantic import BaseModel,ConfigDict,Field
class Input(BaseModel):
    model_config=ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    log:str=Field(min_length=1,max_length=10000)

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A service accepts any dictionary and serializes the provider request with credentials. A permissive model ignores unsupported fields, leaving clients unaware that their intended control was not applied. A valid category lacks evidence.
Test extra fields, wrong types, oversized strings, invalid modes and inconsistent source IDs. Keep error messages stable and free of secret values.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance includes request rejection, response schema conformance and domain evidence checks. OpenAPI documents the same contract that integration tests observe.
SDETs should distinguish 422 input failures from 403 authorization and 503 dependency failures. A typed AI service keeps its outer contract predictable even when an inner model is uncertain.

mistake: A service accepts any dictionary and serializes the provider request with credentials. A permissive model ignores unsupported fields, leaving clients unaware that their intended control was not applied. A valid category lacks evidence.
takeaway: Acceptance includes request rejection, response schema conformance and domain evidence checks.

exercise.prompt: Implement the function in the editor. def request_fields(body):. Use the worked contract, handle the stated boundary cases, and inspect the behavior checks.
exercise.solution:
def request_fields(body):
    return set(body)<={'log','failure_id','mode'} and isinstance(body.get('log'),str) and 1<=len(body['log'])<=10000
exercise.tests:
assert request_fields({'log':'x'})
assert not request_fields({'log':'x','api_key':'secret'})
assert not request_fields({'log':''})
hints: A request model defines which fields a client may supply, their types and bounds.
A service accepts any dictionary and serializes the provider request with credentials.
Use Pydantic ConfigDict(extra='forbid'), bounded strings and closed mode/category enums.
Acceptance includes request rejection, response schema conformance and domain evidence checks.

title: Dependency injection and realistic API test overrides
objectives: Dependency injection and realistic API test overrides
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects dependency injection and realistic api test overrides with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance proves that the fixture and live adapters share the same domain interface, while their execution modes remain visible.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Dependency injection separates routes from concrete provider, retrieval and identity implementations. A test can substitute a controlled adapter while retaining real request parsing, routing and response serialization. This is stronger than testing the route function in isolation with hand-built objects.
Overrides should replace external boundaries, not bypass the application invariant being tested. Mocking authorization to always true cannot establish tenant isolation.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use FastAPI Depends for principal and adapter construction. In tests, supply a fixture provider returning known valid, malformed or refused results, then issue HTTP requests through TestClient/ASGI transport. Assert status, body schema, headers and actual domain effects.
Reset overrides after each test and create fresh state when histories or caches are involved. Keep a separate integration test for actual SDK/protocol wiring where credentials are not required.
sections.code:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client=TestClient(app)
response=client.post('/chat',json={'query':'retry HTTP 429'})
assert response.status_code==200 and response.json()['citations']

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A global dependency override leaks into later tests and disables auth. Tests call classify directly and miss request model validation. A mock returns a convenient dictionary incompatible with the real provider’s typed result.
Test the normalized adapter contract and at least one real serialization path. Include invalid inputs and dependency exceptions so public error behavior is checked.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance proves that the fixture and live adapters share the same domain interface, while their execution modes remain visible. The live adapter test validates the request configuration and closes the async client without making a paid call.
SDETs should retain realistic boundaries: mocking a provider is appropriate for deterministic service behavior; evaluating model correctness requires controlled live evidence.

mistake: A global dependency override leaks into later tests and disables auth. Tests call classify directly and miss request model validation. A mock returns a convenient dictionary incompatible with the real provider’s typed result.
takeaway: Acceptance proves that the fixture and live adapters share the same domain interface, while their execution modes remain visible.

title: Async service capacity: provider I/O versus CPU work
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects async service capacity: provider i/o versus cpu work with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance demonstrates bounded external waits, clean cancellation and stable typed unavailable responses.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Async awaits allow other requests to progress while I/O is pending. They do not make blocking CPU or synchronous network operations nonblocking. Model training and long evaluation should use bounded jobs/workers, while request-time provider calls use asynchronous clients, deadlines and admission controls.
Per-attempt timeouts are not a whole-task deadline. Queue waiting and retries must fit the user's total latency budget.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: The live adapter uses AsyncOpenAI, bounded SDK retries, a maximum output budget and asyncio.wait_for over the entire call. It closes the client in finally. A production service also bounds queued/in-flight work and cancels provider work on client disconnect.

Keep lightweight fixture classification in the route and move expensive fitting into the explicit training commands. Record queue, provider and validation durations separately rather than one unexplained timer.
sections.code:
import asyncio
result=await asyncio.wait_for(provider_call(),timeout=15)
# Close clients and release capacity in finally blocks

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: An async handler invokes a blocking trainer and starves unrelated health requests. A timeout is caught as success with an empty result. Cancellation does not release a semaphore permit.
Inject a slow adapter and verify deadline outcome, cleanup and subsequent healthy requests. Load tests should include concurrent long/short requests and errors, not only the fastest endpoint.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance demonstrates bounded external waits, clean cancellation and stable typed unavailable responses. CPU-heavy work has a separate controlled execution path.

SDETs should assess both latency and correctness under concurrency. A service returning invalid results quickly does not meet performance objectives, and a correct result after the deadline does not complete the intended user task.

mistake: An async handler invokes a blocking trainer and starves unrelated health requests. A timeout is caught as success with an empty result. Cancellation does not release a semaphore permit.
takeaway: Acceptance demonstrates bounded external waits, clean cancellation and stable typed unavailable responses.

exercise.prompt: Implement the function in the editor. def can_admit(in_flight,max_in_flight,queue,max_queue):. Use the worked contract, handle the stated boundary cases, and inspect the behavior checks.
exercise.tests:
assert can_admit(1,2,0,0)
assert not can_admit(2,2,3,3)
assert can_admit(2,2,2,3)
hints: Async awaits allow other requests to progress while I/O is pending.
An async handler invokes a blocking trainer and starves unrelated health requests.
The live adapter uses AsyncOpenAI, bounded SDK retries, a maximum output budget and asyncio.wait_for over the entire call.
Acceptance demonstrates bounded external waits, clean cancellation and stable typed unavailable responses.

title: Health, readiness, OpenAPI and safe error contracts
objectives: Health, readiness, OpenAPI and safe error contracts
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects health, readiness, openapi and safe error contracts with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance includes cheap probes, accurate readiness for the declared mode, typed OpenAPI and safe correlated errors.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Liveness asks whether the process is functioning; readiness asks whether it can serve its required workload. A live process can be unready because a dependency or index is unavailable. OpenAPI describes route contracts for clients, while actual integration checks prove that implementation matches them.
Health probes should be inexpensive and avoid paid model calls. Quality evaluation is a different workflow from operational probing.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Expose a cheap health result and a readiness result naming required mode/dependency state. Test all domain endpoints and request/response models against OpenAPI. Add correlation and timing headers without exposing credentials or raw sensitive errors.

Map malformed input to 422, denied identity/access to 401/403 and controlled dependency failure to 503. Retain internal safe trace references for diagnosis, but do not serialize raw provider exceptions to clients.
sections.code:
# GET /health -> process status
# GET /ready -> readiness for declared fixture/live dependencies
# Inspect /openapi.json and correlate X-Request-ID with safe traces

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A readiness probe always returns ready despite an unavailable required index. A health probe calls the model, causing costs and false restarts during rate limits. Error bodies leak request headers or tokens.
Test health under simulated dependency failure, readiness transitions, public error schemas and secret redaction. Check that every advertised route can be exercised with a known fixture.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance includes cheap probes, accurate readiness for the declared mode, typed OpenAPI and safe correlated errors. Fixture readiness states must not be mistaken for live-provider readiness.
For SDETs, probe and API checks are deterministic operational contracts. They support deployment and recovery while quality metrics separately assess the model's task behavior.

mistake: A readiness probe always returns ready despite an unavailable required index. A health probe calls the model, causing costs and false restarts during rate limits. Error bodies leak request headers or tokens.
takeaway: Acceptance includes cheap probes, accurate readiness for the declared mode, typed OpenAPI and safe correlated errors.

exercise.prompt: Implement the function in the editor. def readiness(required):. Use the worked contract, handle the stated boundary cases, and inspect the behavior checks.
exercise.solution:
def readiness(required):
    return bool(required) and all(value is True for value in required.values())
exercise.tests:
assert readiness({'data':True,'adapter':True})
assert not readiness({'data':True,'adapter':False})
assert not readiness({})
hints: Liveness asks whether the process is functioning; readiness asks whether it can serve its required workload.
A readiness probe always returns ready despite an unavailable required index.
Expose a cheap health result and a readiness result naming required mode/dependency state.
Acceptance includes cheap probes, accurate readiness for the declared mode, typed OpenAPI and safe correlated errors.
exercise.explanation:
def readiness(required):
    return bool(required) and all(value is True for value in required.values())
